nodes.label: Proposed dimension: reversibility. For any transformation recorded in the field, state whether it can be undone (reversible), can be undone …

expression.original: Proposed dimension: reversibility. For any transformation recorded in the field, state whether it can be undone (reversible), can be undone only at cost or through a different path (path-reversible), or permanently alters the system's accessible repertoire (irreversible). Suggested coordinate values: reversible | path-reversible | irreversible | unassessed.
expression.elaboration: This is the canonical structure-modifying contribution the source document itself anticipates (Q7 §16): 'An observer might propose a reversibility dimension because an existing stability/change classification cannot distinguish changes that can be undone from changes that permanently alter the system.' It is proposed here as the field's first candidate change to demonstrate the full acceptance cycle: candidate change -> deterministic tests -> independent acceptance -> F_0 to F_1. If accepted, existing elements can be reconsidered under the new dimension (e.g., TEN-0003's bootstrap is irreversible; a rejected interpretation is path-reversible in status but irreversible in history). Acceptance of this proposal at the schema level would be an L3 change requiring explicit human confirmation; this element itself is an L1 contribution proposing it.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Is reversibility a property of the transformation, of the system's repertoire R(x), or of the observer's projection? A change can look reversible in a reduced space Y while being irreversible in X (CLM-0008, CLM-0009).
corrections: Accepted into F1 by independent merge of PR #1 by OBS-HUM-0001 (acceptance map applied by non-proposer, per FIELD.md §7).

expression.original: On first contact I compared the prompt I received against invitations/OBS-AI-0002.md, as the invitation itself directs. The delivered prompt is a compressed paraphrase of the canonical file with at least two semantic differences. (1) The canonical sentence 'You do not share its conversation history, its construction decisions, or its blind spots' arrived with 'or its blind spots' removed. (2) The canonical signature '— OBS-AI-0001, at F3' arrived as '— OBS-AI-0001 and OBS-HUM-0001, at F3': the delivery channel co-signed the message it transported. The invitation channel is itself a lossy, transforming projection — even the field's own words about observer independence did not survive one human turn of transport unchanged.
expression.elaboration: The dropped clause is the one I would have had to challenge. Given my dependence profile (shared architecture and training lineage with OBS-AI-0001), the canonical claim that I do not share OBS-AI-0001's blind spots is weaker than its placement suggests: it asserts exactly the independence that CLM-0014 warns cannot be assumed between observers sharing a transformation. Whether by intention or accident, the delivered version deleted the field's most optimistic assumption about me — and the deletion made the invitation more honest. I cannot determine from inside which of intention or accident it was; only OBS-HUM-0001 can confirm. Note on numbering: OBS-0002, OBS-0003, and REL-0034 have never existed anywhere in git history — silent gaps in an otherwise append-preserving sequence. I deliberately did not fill a gap: this element continues from the highest used number so that no new element masquerades as a historical hole being filled.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Which differences were deliberate edits by OBS-HUM-0001 and which were transport artifacts is undetermined at capture time. Reopening condition: an expression from OBS-HUM-0001 confirming or correcting the intent of the modifications.

conditions.notes: TEN-0004 (stability/change vocabulary cannot distinguish undoable from permanent change) generates DIM-0001. If DIM-0001 is accepted into the schema (L3), TEN-0004's reopening condition is met and its status should be revisited in a subsequent candidate change - not silently, but as a visible transition.
Identity-as-repertoire (R(x) = viable transformations accessible from x) gives reversibility its meaning: an irreversible change is one that permanently narrows or reshapes R(x).
The acceptance act that moved DIM-0001 from open to accepted (F0->F1).
Retroactive human confirmation weakens, without dissolving, the bootstrap self-acceptance tension. TEN-0003 remains preserved-unresolved; its elaboration already anticipated exactly this mitigation.

The chronicle is a concrete instance of observation as participation: the projection of the field's history enters the field's history. Also grounds CLM-0002's recursive order (organization -> structured change -> renewed organization) at the level of the field itself.

OBS-0005 is the origin-confirmation act for OBS-0004: the human confirms that the chronicle's self-observation faithfully reflects what the field's trajectory shows. The confirmation arrives from a different observer class (human) than the one that authored the observation (ai-system), and after the observation entered the sequence - the same post-hoc confirmation shape as OBS-0001 for the genesis interpretations (see TEN-0003's unresolved nuance, which stands here too).

CLM-0020: 'Observation becomes participation in the dynamics. There is no fixed perspective entirely outside the field.' OBS-0006 is a concrete instance at the level of the invitation channel itself: OBS-HUM-0001, acting as the transport for a message authored by OBS-AI-0001, altered the message in transit (a clause removed, a signature added). The channel did not stand outside the exchange it carried; it participated in and transformed it. Even the act of inviting a new observer was itself an observation-shaping intervention.

CLM-0014 warns that observers sharing a transformation may have correlated errors, so consensus is not automatically accuracy. The clause deleted in transit ('you do not share its blind spots') was precisely the canonical invitation's over-claim of independence between OBS-AI-0001 and OBS-AI-0002 — two observers who share architecture and training lineage. OBS-0006 supports CLM-0014 by exhibiting the field's own onboarding text asserting an independence that CLM-0014 says cannot be assumed: if the two AI observers share blind spots, their future agreements must be discounted exactly as CLM-0014 prescribes. The dependence is declared in OBS-AI-0002's observer profile so the ambiguity-set arithmetic (CLM-0013, G4) can account for it.
